**Best overall: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel, $699 (list $879)**

It has a 1,070Wh LiFePO4 battery, 1,500W AC output and about 24 lbs of weight. It's well reviewed at 4.5 stars across 1.4K ratings, and Talk of the House names it their editor's choice. A full recharge takes 6 to 8 hours of good sun with the one panel. [Amazon listing](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) (this is a search results page, so look for the Jackery 1000 v2 there).

**Other good picks**

|---|---|---|
| Best value at ~1kWh | ALLPOWERS P1800 + 400W panel (1,024Wh, 1,800W). It has twice the panel of most kits in this class. | $731, or $657.90 with code ALLPOWERS26 ([buy](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit)) |
| Well-known alternative at ~1kWh | EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic + 220W (1,024Wh, 1,800W) | $699 ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels)) |
| Home backup (~2kWh) | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 + 2×200W (2,042Wh, 2,200W) | $1,399 ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included)) |
| Home backup, cheaper | BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200W (2,074Wh, 2,600W). It accepts up to 1,000W of panels later. | $1,199, or $1,139 with code AFF5OFF ([buy](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2-200w-solar-kit)) |
| ~3kWh | BLUETTI Elite 300 + 2×200W | $1,599.99 ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels)) |
| Tight budget | ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 + 100W (256Wh, 300W) | $208.99, or $188.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 ([buy](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-volix-p300-100w-solar-kit)) |

**How to choose**
- **Size the battery to what you need to run.** A fridge uses roughly 1 to 1.5kWh a day, so ~1kWh covers a short outage and 2kWh or more is better for multi-day backup.
- **Expect less than the panel's rating.** A folding panel delivers about 60 to 75% of its rated watts in good sun. A 200W panel adds roughly 600 to 750Wh on a clear day.
- **Prefer LiFePO4 batteries.** They last thousands of charge cycles, and every pick above uses them.

**Caveats**
- The Dealectric links go to the brands' official stores, and Dealectric is paid when you use them. Its prices were last checked around Oct 21 to 24, so confirm them at checkout.
- Talk of the House says some kits ship the panels separately from the power station, so check the listing to confirm the panel is in the box.
- Amazon prices and stock change often. The Costco listing for the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 kit ($899.99) was out of stock at the Mountain View warehouse, though it may still ship ([Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html)).

Tell me your budget and what you want to power (camping, a fridge, a CPAP, whole-home backup) and I can narrow this to one pick.
